sourceClassification.preservation: Corrections update the canonical scene override and namespaced correction log through a pinned Core ChangeOperation proposal. P04's generic file producer performs the legacy path mapping; P10 does not create a duplicate speaker-specific importer or writer.

Only a model that improves the deterministic held-out score by at least five percentage points is proposed, with the canonical model file revision as a read precondition. The model is author state; the worker never writes it. P04 owns the generic legacy-path mapping.

Reports and gates are rebuilt from the pinned canonical snapshot. Cache path and stored envelope identity include the snapshot, speaker module and engine versions, shared tokenizer model/version, and adopted-model revision; stale identities are rejected. Training status and outputs are not committed author data.

implementedBehavior: Ports the source CPU attribution pipeline, mention matching, voice-profile hints, speaker-count estimation, clustering and group labeling, override alignment, rule gates, held-out evaluation, correction logging, and the TypeScript logistic reranker/trainer. Shared Lindera analysis is acquired through the host NLP capability; speaker jobs execute in the compiled worker entry and are disposed after each action.

Public actions cover scene attribution, the unresolved/low-confidence confirmation queue, proposal-only speaker and speaker-count corrections, latest evaluation and rule-gate reads, evaluation/gate rebuild, deterministic held-out retraining and gated model-adoption proposals.

R16 character dialogue listing preserves volume/chapter scene order, high/low confidence filtering, optional scene selection, and trailing-limit behavior. Character voice profiles report learned fingerprints, similarity pairs, and stylometric profiles from high-confidence attributed dialogue.

Voice checking composes P06's declared voice-pattern/context-profile checks, learned fingerprint deviations, and stylometric deviations over the same actual scene attributions. It returns the three detailed warning sets and one merged UI list with registered, learned, or stylometric source labels.

The browser contribution renders attribution and correction controls, count proposals, the confirmation queue, character dialogue, voice-profile comparison and similar-character warnings, and evaluation/gate/retraining workflows. Browser acceptance exercises the rendered controls and their registered action boundary.

Every generated public speaker result carries a shared additive identity envelope for the speaker engine/module, shared tokenizer, and the canonical adopted-model file revision (or null when no adopted model is present); legacy provenance fields remain available.

Server imports use pure shared engine constants/types; importing the server module does not execute the worker entry or add a process IPC message listener. Worker IPC is installed only when the compiled worker entry runs in its supervised child.
